unit.can_do_en: talk with the daycare and school about my children.

brief.situation_en: Maria picks up Lucas. Sari works at the daycare.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Hi! I've come to pick up Lucas.

judge.reason: Only register differences: Moi/Hei, mä/minä, 'hakee' vs 'hakemaan'. Same meaning.

lines.speaker: Sari
lines.gloss_en: Hi! He's playing in the yard.

judge.reason: se/hän is a register difference for a person; pihal/pihalla is a dropped ending. Same meaning.

lines.speaker: Sari
lines.text_puhe: Hyvin! Se söi hyvin ja nukku päiväunet.
lines.text_kirja: Hyvin! Hän söi hyvin ja nukkui päiväunet.
lines.gloss_en: Well! He ate well and had a nap.

judge.reason: se/hän and nukku/nukkui are register differences; same content.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Hyvä. Huomenna mä haen sen vähän myöhemmin.
lines.text_kirja: Hyvä. Huomenna minä haen hänet vähän myöhemmin.
lines.gloss_en: Good. Tomorrow I'll pick him up a bit later.

judge.reason: mä/minä and sen/hänet are register differences; same time and action.
Onks/onko is a register difference; same time and question.

lines.speaker: Sari
lines.text_puhe: Joo, me ollaan auki puol kuuteen.
lines.text_kirja: Kyllä, me olemme auki puoli kuuteen.
lines.gloss_en: Yes, we're open until half past five.

judge.reason: Joo/kyllä, ollaan/olemme and puol/puoli are register differences; same meaning, open until half past five.

forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.

Adds -i for the past and -n for 'I': tulla becomes tulin.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to fetch, to pick up, to apply
forms.why_en: After tulla 'to come', the verb takes -maan: hakemaan. Speech says hakee.
Speech uses se for a person. Books write hän.
Leikkiä takes the doubled last vowel for he or she: leikkii.
Adds -lla for 'in' an open place: piha becomes pihalla. Speech shortens -lla to -l: pihalla becomes pihal.

Books write nukkui. Speech drops the last i: nukku.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to fetch, to pick up, to apply
forms.why_en: Hakea changes to hae- and takes -n for 'I': haen.
Hän takes -t when it is the person you pick up: hänet. Speech uses se and says sen.

Adds -ltä to a number to give a clock time. Viisi changes its s to d first: viideltä, 'at five'.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.

Puoli neljä means 'half to four', so 3.30. Speech drops the last i: puol.
